Hi Luke — great to see the worksheet, thanks. Looping in Marissa (CS / Implementation) and Ben (Ops) to start drafting a pragmatic activation plan and the netops checklist.

Quick responses to your asks:
- We'll propose a pool S3: mix that routes interactive chat traffic to a reserved set of A100-style instances (for lower latency on 70B) and a separate quantized T4/RTX pool for 13B cost efficiency.
- For marketing spikes, we typically suggest a burst buffer of 15-25% above the reserved commit for the first 60–90 days while traffic stabilizes, combined with aggressive prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Primary region us-west-2 + automatic fallback to us-east-1 is straightforward; we'll call out expected cross-region replication lag and KV cache coldness in the plan.
- Lead time: reserved capacity commits for specific instance families typically need 3–6 weeks to secure in a new region. Short term we can provide temporary burst/spot capacity while the reserved pool is negotiated.

Marissa and Ben — can you propose:
1) A recommended initial pool spec (GPU types, count, estimated tokens/sec capacity)
2) Autoscale thresholds (queue depth, cpu/gpu util, cooling windows) and a burst policy draft
3) Netops prerequisites (VPC peering, IP ranges, maintenance blackout windows)
4) A minimal test plan for a blue-green activation and failback test

Luke — once we have that, Marissa will draft an activation timeline and I can coordinate SOW/Procurement with your team.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Hi team — put together a first-pass activation/implementation playbook below (high level) based on the worksheet and prior turnups. Happy to iterate.

1) Initial pool recommendation
- Primary pool (us-west-2): 8 x 80GB GPUs for 70B models (target p95 <=200ms); 12 x 32GB GPUs (quantized) serving 13B family for cost efficiency.
- Warm buffer: keep 2 instances of each group in warm standby (fast spin-up) for immediate bursts.
- Estimated effective throughput: ~1.1M tokens/minute aggregate (mixed load).

2) Autoscale & burst policy (draft)
- Scaling metrics: queue length (requests), GPU % utilization, and token backlog. Primary triggers: queue > 40 for 30s or GPU util > 78% for 60s.
- Scale unit: add/remove 1 instance per scale action; cooldown 90s.
- Burst capacity: allow temporary +20% node pool (non-reserved) for bursts up to 15 minutes; if bursts exceed 3x baseline for >20m, automatically route to cold fallback pool and trigger alert to ops.
- Canary rollout: enable traffic shadowing for first two weeks, 5% live traffic, ramp to 25% then full cutover.

3) Regional fallback behavior
- KV/prefix cache will be warm in primary; after failover to us-east-1 expect 200–400ms additional cold-start penalty for large context sessions. Recommend session affinity TTL of 10 minutes to minimize cross-region churn.

4) Test plan & acceptance
- Blue-green activation with synthetic traffic ramp: 0.1x -> 0.5x -> 1x -> 1.5x baseline over 4 hours, validate p95 SLAs and error rates <0.5%
- Failback test: simulate primary outage and validate fallback completes within 60s and session degradation metrics recorded

5) Deliverables and timeline (target)
- Week 0–1: finalize SOW and procurement signoff
- Week 2–3: provision reserved instances and VPC peering windows
- Week 4: warm pool and smoke tests
- Week 5: staged rollout, monitoring handoff, runbook delivery

Action items for Novagen: share a 48-hour sample traffic trace (obfuscated) and confirm procurement lead / netops contact for peering windows.

Marissa
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference

Adding a few ops-level constraints and questions.

Netops prerequisites:
- VPC peering: please provide allowed CIDR ranges and preferred peering window. Our typical maintenance blackout for peering is Tue/Wed 02:00–06:00 UTC; we can be flexible but need a 72-hour notice.
- Egress/IP allowlist: will share a signed JSON list of IP blocks once pool is provisioned.
- Monitoring endpoints: we'll provide metrics endpoints and a short Prometheus scrape guide; confirm if you need cust-managed collectors.

Operational guardrails:
- We recommend a max 25% of total baseline capacity for ad-hoc burst unless a commercial burst add-on is purchased — otherwise burst may rely on spot/ephemeral capacity which carries preemption risk.
- Bring-forward window for reserved SKU swaps (if you later change GPU families) is 4 weeks in-region.

Runbooks & DR:
- We'll provide runbook drafts (activation, rollback, scaledown) and a one-page escalation matrix. Marissa will own runbook signoff with your engineering manager during Week 4 tests.

Procurement note: procurement@novagen.com — we'll need a signed SOW and security addendum before reserved capacity provisioning. If you can share a procurement point person and any internal PO timelines that helps.

Ben Carter
Principal Cloud Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
